C — Definitions (Section 1)

Domain: handbook definitional vocabulary for first-time regular passenger-car applicants.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01

Careless driving covers committing two or more moving violations in one continuous drive, or one moving violation while distracted by an in-vehicle non-driving activity such as looking for an object or personal grooming [A01].
Why it matters: it is the only multi-violation behavioral definition in this section.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01

Blind spots are roadway areas not visible in mirrors during operation, while head checks mean turning the head and looking over the shoulder toward the intended movement [A01].
Why it matters: pairs a hazard concept with its named countermeasure.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01

An alcohol restricted driver is barred from operating with any alcohol in the body following an alcohol-related conviction, suspension or revocation [A01].
Why it matters: zero-tolerance status is stricter than a general limit.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02

An interlock restricted driver may operate only a vehicle fitted with an ignition interlock system, which is a constant monitor requiring a breath sample to start and run the vehicle [A02].
Why it matters: links the driver status to the required device.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01

Cancellation ends a license granted through error or fraud, after application for another state credential, or after required consent is withdrawn [A01].
Why it matters: distinct from punishment-based withdrawals.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A03

Revocation ends the privilege to drive, suspension withdraws it temporarily, denial withholds driving privilege, and disqualification withdraws commercial privilege temporarily or permanently [A03].
Why it matters: four-way status contrast is highly confusable.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01

Extreme DUI includes breath or blood alcohol at or above the stated higher threshold, or the lower alcohol threshold combined with measurable controlled substance, or two or more non-excepted controlled substances [A01].
Why it matters: captures the tiered evidentiary definition.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01

A commercial license covers vehicles at or above the stated heavy weight threshold, vehicles built for the stated larger passenger count, plus hazardous materials, doubles or triples, tankers and school buses [A01].
Why it matters: scope rule with vehicle, occupancy and cargo branches.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02

A low-speed vehicle is a four-wheeled electric vehicle capped at the stated low maximum speed and four occupants including the driver, excluding golf carts and off-highway vehicles [A02].
Why it matters: speed plus occupancy plus exclusions.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02

A personal motorized mobility device has two non-tandem ground wheels, steering and stopping under normal use, a motor capped at the stated small power limit, and a standing deck [A02].
Why it matters: four-element device test.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A03

A roundabout is a circular intersection with counterclockwise flow [A03].
Why it matters: single-sentence direction rule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A03

A provisional license is a Utah license issued to a person under the stated younger-adult age threshold [A03].
Why it matters: age-gated credential type.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A03

A temporary license allows driving privileges up to the stated half-year period and is unavailable to driving privilege card holders [A03].
Why it matters: duration plus eligibility exception.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02

Division means the Driver License Division of the Department of Public Safety, operator means a person in actual physical control, and highway means the full width between property lines available for vehicular travel [A02].
Why it matters: foundational authority, actor and roadway terms.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0012]

Misconceptions: cancellation equals suspension; revocation equals temporary loss; any alcohol restriction equals interlock requirement; roundabout flow is clockwise; provisional status ends at a different birthday.

Mnemonics: C-R-S-D ladder for Cancellation, Revocation, Suspension, Denial by severity and cause; ARD means no alcohol while IRD means interlock required.

Glossary: ARD; IRD; IID; CDL; DPC; provisional license; temporary license; blind spots; head checks; traffic check; roundabout; highway; operator; Division.
